zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-ʿĀdiyāt
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿والعادِياتِ ضَبْحًا﴾ ("by the chargers, panting"): by al-ʿādiyāt here the horses are meant. This is an oath, whose answer is ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾ [al-ʿĀdiyāt: 6] ("the human being is surely ungrateful to his Lord").
And His saying: ﴿ضَبْحًا﴾: its meaning is "by the chargers that pant a panting"; and their panting is the sound of their insides when they run.

zajjaj:2-2.t: ﴿فالمُورِياتِ قَدْحًا﴾ ("and the strikers of sparks"): when the horses run at night and their hooves strike the stones, sparks of fire are struck from them.

zajjaj:3-3.t: ﴿فالمُغِيراتِ صُبْحًا﴾ ("and the raiders at dawn"): the horses are meant. It has come in the exegesis that it was a raiding party (sariyya) of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ against Kinda.

zajjaj:4-4.t: ﴿فَأثَرْنَ بِهِ نَقْعًا﴾ ("stirring up dust thereby"): ”اَلنَّقْعُ“ is dust. He said ”بِهِ“ ("thereby") although the place had not been mentioned before, but there is evidence for it in the discourse; the meaning is: "they stirred up nuqʿ in the place of their running", that is, dust.

zajjaj:5-5.t: ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا﴾ ("and penetrating thereby into a host"): the reading is ﴿فَوَسَطْنَ﴾, that is, they went into the middle of the place. If one said ”فَوَسَّطْنَ بِهِ جَمْعًا“ it would be permissible, except that I know of no one who read it so.

zajjaj:6-6.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنَّ الإنْسانَ لِرَبِّهِ لَكَنُودٌ﴾: its meaning is "surely ungrateful"; by that the unbeliever is meant.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
﴿وَإنَّهُ لِحُبِّ الخَيْرِ لَشَدِيدٌ﴾ ("and he is, in love of wealth, surely intense"): the meaning of ”لَشَدِيدٌ“ is "surely miserly", that is: and he, on account of love of wealth, is surely miserly. Ṭarafa said:
أرى المَوْتَ يَعْتامُ الكِرامَ ويَصْطَفِي ∗∗∗ عَقِيلَةَ مالِ الباخِلِ المُتَشَدِّدِ
(I see death choosing the generous, and selecting the choicest of the wealth of the tight-fisted miser [al-mutashaddid].)

zajjaj:9-9.t: And His saying: ﴿أفَلا يَعْلَمُ إذا بُعْثِرَ ما في القُبُورِ﴾ ("does he not know, when what is in the graves is scattered out?"): ”بُعْثِرَ“ and ”بُحْثِرَ“ have one meaning; and the meaning is: "does he not know, when the dead are resurrected?"

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿إنَّ رَبَّهم بِهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَخَبِيرٌ﴾ ("their Lord, on that Day, is surely fully aware of them"): Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is aware of them on that day and on other days; but the meaning is: "Allah will requite them for their unbelief on that day", and He does not requite them except by His knowledge of their deeds. Similar to it is: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُ اللَّهُ ما في قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 63] ("those are the ones of whom Allah knows what is in their hearts"), whose meaning is: those are the ones whose requital He leaves aside. [Translator's note: so in the source, «يَتْرُكُ مُجازاتِهِمْ»; the sense intended may be that He does not leave aside requiting them.]
